newsitem.title: UK: FX in Europe - Yen weakness gives dlr helping hand.
newsitem.headline: FX in Europe - Yen weakness gives dlr helping hand.

text.p: The dollar ended higher in Europe on Thursday as broad-based yen weakness pushed dollar/yen higher, leading dollar/mark up along the way, traders said.

The mark has staged an impulsive recovery from two-year lows just above 62 yen to a two-week high of 63.80 in four days amid mark short-covering versus European currencies and the yen, dealers said. The yen also weakened sharply against sterling.
The prospect that German interest rates might rise before Japanese has increased the appeal of the mark.

Even though mark/yen strength tends to weigh on dollar/mark, the dollar's ability to hold above important technical support encouraged traders to buy it at the lows after its three-pfennig slide on Wednesday, dealers said.
"In the absence of big news to move the dollar, trade was quite technical - and the main engine behind the dollar's move higher was the weakness of the yen," said a dealer at a UK bank.

Dealers were encouraged to buy dollars at the lows after it held above key resistance at 1.8275/65 because a break below that would have confirmed a bearish chart pattern. The dollar hit a session low at 1.8297 marks.

A modest rise in U.S. industrial production in July coupled with a drop in capacity utilisation had little impact on the dollar. The data confirmed the established picture of healthy third quarter growth with benign inflation, analysts said.
Industrial production rose 0.2 percent in July, in line with expectations, after an unrevised 0.3 percent rise in June.
Capacity utilisation fell to 83.1 percent from a downwardly revised 83.3 percent. The market had expected the rate of capacity use to be flat.

On the European crosses, the mark remained firm - though off peaks - after receiving a boost on Wednesday from a warning by the Bundesbank that as German inflation had picked up it would steer policy to ensure price stability was maintained.
Analysts said the mark was firmer amid rising speculation short-term German interest rates may rise.
"The main theme in continental Europe is German rate fears... That should give the deutschemark some support," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.

The mark rose to near four-week highs against the Norwegian and Swedish crowns. General mark strength combined with jitters ahead of Norway's September election and thin summer volumes to give the mark a leg-up against the Nordics, dealers said.
The mark was at 4.1415/45 Norwegian crowns, of its 4.1555 peak but up from 4.1470/1500 in late European trade on Wednesday.
Mark/Swedish crown reversed its gains in late trade though and was at 4.3600/30, down from a high of 4.3730 and compared with 4.3635/65 at the previous close.

Sterling/mark gained on the back of the firmer dollar/mark. It stood at 2.9276/86 from 2.9008/18. Cable was at $1.5870/80 from $1.5841/46. Sterling/yen surged to a late high of 187.46 from 183.31 at the previous close here.
In Asia, the Indonesian rupiah slid to a record low versus the dollar at 2,815 after Indonesia's central bank abolished its intervention band. It was last quoted at 2770.00/2800.00.
